from slugs import slugify


def test_precomposed_accented_phrase():
    assert slugify("Caf\u00e9 d\u00e9j\u00e0 vu") == "cafe-deja-vu"


def test_decomposed_combining_acute_matches_precomposed():
    decomposed = "cafe" + "\u0301"
    assert slugify(decomposed) == slugify("caf\u00e9")
    assert slugify(decomposed) == "cafe"


def test_output_is_lowercase_ascii_only():
    result = slugify("Caf\u00e9 d\u00e9j\u00e0 vu")
    assert result == result.lower()
    assert result.isascii()


def test_ascii_word_separation_preserved():
    assert slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world"
    assert slugify("foo   bar") == "foo-bar"
    assert slugify("a---b") == "a-b"


def test_leading_and_trailing_dashes_trimmed():
    assert slugify("  Hello, World!  ") == "hello-world"
    assert slugify("---abc---") == "abc"
    assert slugify("!!!") == ""


def test_plain_ascii_behavior_unchanged():
    assert slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world"
    assert slugify("") == ""
    assert slugify("already-slug") == "already-slug"

patches.rationale: The current slugify lowercases then strips all non-[a-z0-9] characters, so accented letters like 'é' are dropped entirely (e.g. 'Café déjà vu' -> 'caf-d-j-vu'). The fix normalizes to NFKD so precomposed accents decompose into base letter + combining mark, then drops combining marks, yielding ASCII base letters. Lowercasing is applied after normalization so uppercase accented letters also decompose correctly. Existing ASCII word-separation (runs of non-alphanumerics -> single '-') and dash trimming are preserved. New regression tests are added in a new file; existing tests are untouched.
